title: JavaScript Performance Optimization Applied Check
description: Apply JavaScript performance concepts by choosing optimizations for input handlers, rendering, caching, lazy loading, workers, network cost, and DevTools profiling scenarios.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A search box filters a large list on every keystroke, and users only need results after they pause typing. Which technique is most appropriate?

options.text: Run the search twice per keystroke

questions.explanation: Debouncing waits for typing to pause before running the search, reducing unnecessary work.

questions.prompt: A scroll progress bar should update while the user scrolls, but not on every scroll event. Which option is best?

options.text: Throttle the update or schedule it with `requestAnimationFrame()`
Move the DOM update into JSON

questions.explanation: Throttling or `requestAnimationFrame()` keeps visual feedback regular without running on every event.

options.text: It mixes DOM writes and layout reads repeatedly, which can cause layout thrashing
It uses a `for...of` loop, which never works with DOM elements
Width can only be set with `setTimeout()`

questions.explanation: Writing layout-affecting styles and then reading layout values in a loop can force repeated layout calculations.

questions.prompt: You need to add 1,000 list items to the DOM. Which approach usually reduces repeated live DOM work?

options.text: Build the nodes in a `DocumentFragment`, then append the fragment
Append and remove each item three times

questions.explanation: A `DocumentFragment` lets you build many nodes before inserting them into the live DOM once.

questions.prompt: Which function is a good candidate for memoization?

options.text: An expensive pure function called repeatedly with the same arguments
A function that must always fetch fresh server data

questions.explanation: Memoization works best when the result is stable for the same inputs and recalculation is expensive.

options.text: The cache can grow forever and increase memory usage

questions.explanation: A `Map` keeps strong references. Without limits or invalidation, cache memory can grow indefinitely.

questions.prompt: A large admin-only editor is included in the initial JavaScript bundle, but most users never open it. What is a practical optimization?

options.text: Load the editor with dynamic `import()` only when needed
Run the editor code on every page load twice
Move the editor into a global variable named `fast`

questions.explanation: Dynamic import can defer rarely used code, reducing initial bundle work.

questions.prompt: What should you add when lazy loading an important UI panel?

options.text: A hidden alert in every module

questions.explanation: Lazy-loaded code can take time or fail, so the UI should handle waiting and errors clearly.

questions.prompt: A JavaScript animation repeatedly changes an element's `left` style and causes choppy movement. Which change is often better?
questions.explanation: `transform` is often cheaper for animation than layout-affecting properties, and `requestAnimationFrame()` aligns updates with painting.

questions.prompt: A CPU-heavy file parser freezes the UI for several seconds. Which optimization may keep the main thread responsive?

options.text: Move the parsing work to a Web Worker
Run the parser from a click handler twice
Put the file contents in CSS

questions.explanation: A Web Worker can run CPU-heavy JavaScript on a background thread so the main thread can stay responsive.

questions.prompt: Which work is a reasonable use of `requestIdleCallback()`?

options.text: Optional low-priority preloading after important work is done
Critical form submission that must happen immediately
Blocking user input until idle time appears

questions.explanation: `requestIdleCallback()` is for low-priority work that can wait and should not block important interactions.

questions.prompt: An API response returns 5 MB of data, but the page only displays names and IDs. What should you consider first?

options.text: Request only the fields or page of data needed if the API supports it
Store the entire response in every DOM node

questions.explanation: Reducing response size can improve network transfer and parsing time.

questions.prompt: A route loads a large amount of unused JavaScript. Which DevTools feature can help reveal unused code?
questions.explanation: Coverage tools show unused JavaScript and CSS for the current page or interaction.

questions.prompt: A page gets slower over time after navigating between screens. Which issue should you investigate?

options.text: Memory leaks such as retained DOM nodes, timers, listeners, or growing caches
Whether all variables are named with one letter
Whether the page has enough blank lines

questions.explanation: Growing memory usage can cause slowdowns and garbage collection pauses over time.

questions.prompt: After making a performance change, what should you do next?

options.text: Measure again and compare with the original problem
Assume it worked because the code looks clever
Make ten unrelated changes before testing

questions.explanation: Performance work should be verified by measuring before and after focused changes.
